<x_0.0078><y_0.0>LEO I.  gentle sudorific ; thorax marked with a large depressed circular spot ; abdomen oval ; legs equal.<x_0.8203><y_0.0437><class_Text>

<x_0.2402><y_0.0445>7. _Eyes placed thus,_ :<x_0.6064><y_0.0641><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0264><y_0.0695>Black, thorax marked with a white line on the back. * dorsal: 79. A native of Britain.<x_0.9434><y_0.1039><class_Text>

<x_0.0273><y_0.0992>Marked with triangular black spots on the back of tarantula, the abdomen ; the legs spotted with black. 34. A native of the south of Europe, particularly Italy and Barbary. It is found in caverus in argillaceous soil ; its bite was formerly supposed to be curable by nothing but music ; though it occasions a great deal of pain, it is almost never fatal.<x_0.9502><y_0.2016><class_Text>

<x_0.252><y_0.2031>8. _Eyes placed thus,_ ...<x_0.6348><y_0.2273><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0322><y_0.2297>Oval and oblong ; thorax hairy, white ; abdomen and pulchra. legs black, marked with yellow bands. 32. A native of Europe.<x_0.9355><y_0.2789><class_Text>

<x_0.2188><y_0.2883>9. _Eyes placed thus,_<x_0.5205><y_0.307><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0352><y_0.3219>Black, abdomen oval, forehead white, and leaps on goezii. its prey. 84. It is to be found frequently in woods about Vienna ; abdomen marked with two compressed dots.<x_0.9209><y_0.3828><class_Text>

<x_0.248><y_0.3797>10. _Eyes placed thus,_ :<x_0.6357><y_0.4><class_Section-header>

<x_0.041><y_0.4055>Thorax orbicular and convex, with a transverse cen-aviculartral excavation. 31. It is a native of South America, among trees, where it preys upon the larger insects, and even small birds, dropping into their nests, and sucking their blood and eggs ; it is of so enormous a size, that its fangs may be compared to the talons of a hawk, and its eyes are very large.<x_0.958><y_0.5117><class_Text>

<x_0.2529><y_0.5203>11. _Eyes placed thus,_ ...<x_0.625><y_0.5391><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0469><y_0.5531>Of a grayish rusty colour, and slightly clouded ; tho-truncate. rax globular, and slightly heart-shaped ; abdomen some-what triangular, and marked with a faint longitudinal cross. 85. A native of Europe, on oak and other trees ; abdomen marked with four impressed dots on the back ; papillae three.<x_0.9551><y_0.6445><class_Text>

<x_0.2559><y_0.6539>12. _Eyes placed thus,_ :<x_0.6484><y_0.6727><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0518><y_0.6797>Abdomen oval, obtusely conic behind, variegated convica. with brown and white ; beneath black. 86. A native of Europe, among bushes ; it spins and spreads out a web, to the surface of which it attaches the insects it has ensnared, after it has sucked out their juice. Tho-rax black, slightly tinged with rusty colour, and nearly double behind ; legs gray, marked with brown rings ; abdomen marked with a whitish spot, beneath resem-bling a horse shoe ; papillae four.<x_0.9346><y_0.8148><class_Text>

<x_0.2178><y_0.8211>13. _Eyes placed thus,_ ...<x_0.5273><y_0.8406><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0547><y_0.8398>Hairy ; body oval, black, variegated with brown. albifras. 99. A native of Europe.<x_0.9639><y_0.8773><class_Text>

<x_0.2344><y_0.8797>B. _Eyes six, placed thus,_ ...<x_0.6807><y_0.8984><class_Section-header>

<x_0.0586><y_0.8992>Abdomen greenish, the sides yellow. 30. A na- somies lata.<x_0.9629><y_0.9344><class_Text>

<x_0.7354><y_0.9273>C. _Eyes_<x_0.8506><y_0.9445><class_Page-footer>
